Preprocess raw single-cell data into clone labels

Source: R/preprocess.R
preprocess_sc.Rd

End-to-end preprocessing for users who only have a raw count matrix: quality control, normalisation, variable-feature selection, PCA, and clustering, followed by a QC report. No tissue-specific thresholds are required; the QC fences adapt to each patient's own distribution.

Usage

preprocess_sc(
  counts,
  patient_labels,
  sample_labels = NULL,
  nmads = 5,
  min_genes = 200,
  max_mito = 25,
  max_genes = NULL,
  skip_qc = FALSE,
  remove_doublets = FALSE,
  exclude_markers = NULL,
  exclude_min_expr = 1,
  nfeatures = 2000,
  dims = 20,
  method = c("umap", "tsne"),
  resolution = 0.8,
  min_clone_cells = 10,
  integrate = c("auto", "none", "harmony"),
  cluster_scope = c("global", "patient"),
  seed = 42,
  progress_cb = NULL
)

Arguments

counts

Matrix (genes as rows, cells as columns) or a Seurat object. Raw counts are expected; normalised values trigger a warning because they would be normalised twice.

patient_labels

Character vector, one entry per cell, giving the patient a cell belongs to. Names are matched to colnames(counts).

sample_labels

Character vector, one entry per cell, giving the sample or batch a cell belongs to. Required only when a patient has multiple samples. Default = NULL.

nmads

Numeric. Width of the MAD-based QC fence, in median absolute deviations. Default = 5. Tumour tissue has genuinely higher mitochondrial content and larger cells than blood, so a 3-MAD fence removes real cells: against CellRanger's own calls on a real lung squamous carcinoma sample, 5 MAD recovers ~88% of its cells versus ~78% at 3 MAD, with precision unchanged.

min_genes

Integer. Minimum detected genes per cell. Default = 200.

max_mito

Numeric. Hard cap on the mitochondrial fraction (%). The effective threshold is the smaller of this and the MAD fence. Default = 25.

max_genes

Integer. Fixed upper bound on detected genes per cell. When NULL (default) the bound is estimated per patient as median + nmads * MAD, which is what removes empty droplets and high-complexity doublets. Set it to reproduce a fixed threshold such as the 2,500 genes used in most tutorials.

skip_qc

Logical. When TRUE, the MAD fences are not applied and every cell is kept; the QC table then only describes the input. This reproduces the original PERCEPTION pipeline, which expects an already-curated matrix (e.g. malignant cells downloaded from a paper), where an extra per-patient fence only perturbs the result. Default FALSE – raw 10x data always needs the fences.

remove_doublets

Logical. When TRUE, cells classified as doublets by scDblFinder are removed after QC, one patient at a time. Doublets can pass every QC threshold – they have normal gene counts and mitochondrial fractions – yet they inflate the high-complexity tail and can form a spurious "resistant clone" made of two fused clones. Requires the optional scDblFinder package; without it the step is skipped with a warning. Default = FALSE, because detection is probabilistic and should be opted into.

exclude_markers

Optional named list of gene vectors, e.g. list(immune = c("PTPRC", "CD3D"), stromal = c("COL1A1")). Cells whose strongest marker-set score reaches exclude_min_expr are removed before clustering. This is an exclusion rule for reducing non-target cells, not a tumour-cell classifier: epithelial markers do not imply malignancy. Default = NULL (keep all cells).

exclude_min_expr

Numeric. Mean log-normalised expression a cell must reach in a marker set to be excluded. Default = 1.

nfeatures

Integer. Number of variable features used for PCA. Default = 2000.

dims

Integer. Number of principal components. Capped automatically for small datasets. Default = 20.

method

Character. 2D embedding for visualisation: "umap" (default) or "tsne". Clustering itself always runs on the PCA embedding; this only changes the coordinates returned in cell_labels.

resolution

Numeric. Clustering resolution. Default = 0.8.

min_clone_cells

Integer. Clones with fewer cells are kept but marked cluster_size_class = "small". Default = 10.

integrate

Character. Sample integration strategy within a patient: "auto" (default) applies harmony when a patient has multiple samples, "none" never integrates, "harmony" behaves like "auto". Only used when cluster_scope = "patient".

cluster_scope

Character. "global" (default) clusters all cells together, matching the original PERCEPTION method, so one clone can span several patients. "patient" clusters inside each patient only, so clone labels are patient-specific. Identical for a single-patient dataset.

seed

Integer. Random seed. Default = 42.

progress_cb

Optional function called as progress_cb(phase, i, n) between stages. Used to drive progress bars in the Shiny app.

Value

A list with:

cell_labels

Data frame with cell_id, clone_id, clone_key (unique "patient@clone" key), patient, cluster_size_class ("large" / "small", a cell-count category and nothing more), and dim_1/dim_2. This is the clone_labels argument of prepare_data().

qc

Data frame. Per-patient QC summary, including n_marker_removed when exclude_markers was used and n_doublet_removed when remove_doublets = TRUE.

qc_metrics

Data frame. Per-cell QC metrics before filtering.

excluded_cells

Data frame. Cells removed by exclude_markers (columns cell_id, set, score); empty when no marker filtering was requested.

doublet_cells

Data frame. Cells removed by remove_doublets (columns cell_id, patient, score); empty when the step was not requested or no doublets were found.

used_harmony

Logical. Whether harmony was applied.

label_source

Character. Always "auto_cluster".

Details

Clustering is performed on a shared PCA embedding. By default (cluster_scope = "global") every cell is clustered together, which is what the original PERCEPTION method does: a clone is a transcriptional state that can appear in several patients. With cluster_scope = "patient" neighbours are searched inside each patient only, so a clone can never span two patients – useful when clone labels are meant to be patient-specific. For a single-patient dataset the two settings are identical.

When a patient has more than one sample (e.g. longitudinal biopsies) and cluster_scope = "patient", harmony is applied inside that patient to prevent one biological clone from being split in two by a technical batch effect. harmony is an optional dependency: without it, the step is skipped with a warning.

What "clone" means here

In the cell-level workflow, clone labels are operationally defined by transcriptomic clustering. Cells are grouped by transcriptional similarity within each patient, and the resulting cluster assignments are used as surrogate clone labels for downstream analysis. These labels do not necessarily represent genetically validated clonal populations and should not be interpreted as evidence of shared genomic ancestry. CNV- or genotype-based evidence is required to call true clones.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
  labels <- preprocess_sc(counts, patient_labels = cell_patients)
  prepared <- prepare_data(
    expression_matrix = counts,
    clone_labels = labels$cell_labels
  )
} # }
